Subject: Demo scheduling — clarify ISO vs local time in calendar invite
Attachments: current-invite.ics (text/calendar)

Hi Kenji / Grace —

Thanks for the quick interest in Redwood Inference. Would love to get a 30-minute intro/demo on the platform and how it could help HarborTech reduce per-token inference costs while meeting latency SLAs. Below are a few candidate slots (I listed local times + UTC to avoid confusion):

- Tokyo (JST): Tue, 21 Dec — 10:30–11:00 JST (2026-12-21T01:30Z)
- Singapore (SGT): Tue, 21 Dec — 09:30–10:00 SGT (2026-12-21T01:30Z)
- Sydney (AEDT): Tue, 21 Dec — 12:30–13:00 AEDT (2026-12-21T02:30Z)

I attached a calendar invite (current-invite.ics). Quick note — my calendar export used an ISO/UTC timestamp, which some clients show as a different local date depending on timezone. If any of the proposed times look like they fall on the wrong local day for you, tell me which city/time you prefer and I will resend an invite explicitly labeled with the city and TZ.

Prefer one of the slots above? Otherwise, send a couple of windows that work for your team and I’ll accommodate.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks, Rafael —

Quick question: the ICS my assistant imported shows the event as "2026-12-21T00:30Z" and our calendar client converted that to 09:30 on Dec 21 for Singapore but to 00:30 on Dec 22 for Tokyo (his words: it moved to the next day). That would put the Tokyo time outside our working hours.

Is the intended Tokyo local time Dec 21 10:30 JST (which is what your mail text says) or did the invite actually encode a UTC time that ends up as late-night for us?

We can do the morning slot if it’s actually 10:30 JST on Dec 21. Could you resend with explicit local TZ labels in the event?

Hi Kenji — thanks for the flag and sorry for the confusion.

You're right — I exported the invite using a UTC timestamp (ISO8601) and some clients then show a different local date. I should've attached a calendar with TZID (explicit timezone) and a clear human-readable line for each city.

Corrected — I just attached a new invite (invite-TYO-SIN-SYD.ics) that encodes the event in each local zone and updates the display name. For clarity, here are the exact local times you should see:

- Tokyo (JST): Tue, 21 Dec — 10:30–11:00 JST (UTC+09:00)
- Singapore (SGT): Tue, 21 Dec — 09:30–10:00 SGT (UTC+08:00)
- Sydney (AEDT): Tue, 21 Dec — 12:30–13:00 AEDT (UTC+11:00)

Notes:
- I added "(Tokyo time)" / "(Singapore time)" into the event title so recipients see the city immediately.
- Also attached our HarborTech security pack you requested earlier (harbortech-security-sheet.pdf).

Sofia — could you please resend the corrected invite from our shared Redwood calendar and confirm the ICS includes TZID lines? Thanks.

Kenji / Grace — can you confirm which local city/time you will accept and I’ll finalize.

Cheers,
Rafael
